principles.rule: Search already-public sources for direct observations before constructing a modeled synthesis.
Preserve source projections separately and never relabel them as modeled or realized values.
Model only decision-relevant metrics with cited inputs, a reproducible formula, defensible scope, and disclosed uncertainty.
When modeling eligibility is not met, document the unresolved evidence gap and analytical limit rather than manufacturing a value or requesting nonpublic data.
Do not send public-records requests, private data requests, surveys, questionnaires, or other solicitations; use already-public evidence and reproducible modeled synthesis only.
Never infer facility values from county, company, campus, utility, or multi-county totals without an explicit allocation model.
Exclude modeled outputs from sourced-record counts, canonical claims, and realized-benefit totals.
Apply identical evidence and uncertainty rules to benefits and costs.
Keep contribution estimates distinct from causal effects.
Multiplier models require a named source, model and version, geography, vintage, local-purchase assumption, and separated direct, indirect, and induced channels.
Do not sum overlapping modeled outputs, source observations, projections, contribution channels, or nested totals.
Keep national-security narratives outside local economic totals unless a sourced quantitative model defines the local channel and scope.
